## 2025-03-01 - DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
**Vulnerability:** The application was directly rendering unsanitized user-generated rich text HTML content from `src/admin/BlogEditor.tsx` directly into the DOM using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on both the frontend `src/pages/BlogPostPage.tsx` and the live preview component inside the editor.
**Learning:** React's built-in protections against XSS do not apply when explicitly using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Because blog posts accept raw HTML (generated by a WYSIWYG editor or raw input), an attacker could inject malicious scripts `<script>` or event handlers `onload=` into the post content, executing arbitrary JavaScript in viewers' browsers.
**Prevention:** Always sanitize any untrusted HTML content string using `DOMPurify.sanitize(htmlString)` before passing it into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Additionally, ensure fallback HTML elements provided to DOMPurify use standard `class` attributes instead of React's `className`, as DOMPurify will strip invalid HTML attributes.
